### Pass 505: The Amber Cinder Horizon

This pass extends endgame horizons and legacy frontiers with the amber cinder horizon. It is a proposal over the current authority owned by UnifiedEndingResolver, CampaignLegacySystem, campaign, faction, diplomacy, expedition, colony, ShelterArchiveSystem, and ending-route owners. The named factions and places are provisional labels, not catalog facts. Start with a source, data, consumer, and ownership audit; if an existing record already expresses the idea, fold this material into that record or stop. The player should make a legible choice that affects a practical task, a remembered relationship, a route, or a late-game interpretation.

#### 1. Premise evidence

Record the exact source path, API or JSON family, event producer, host route, and current plan entry that justify the amber cinder horizon. Name one absent seam and one collision to check. A proposal remains tagged unresolved until the premise is reproduced against current source.

#### 2. Owner contract

Route the command through UnifiedEndingResolver, CampaignLegacySystem, campaign, faction, diplomacy, expedition, colony, ShelterArchiveSystem, and ending-route owners. Define the input, output, refusal, fallback, and event key. Panels, maps, and prose consume the projection and never become a second ledger, graph, clock, route registry, roster, or ending resolver.

#### 3. Player action

Give the player inspect, ask, compare, repair, invite, ration, disclose, wait, or leave choices around the amber cinder horizon. Show cost before commitment, allow a respectful refusal, and provide recovery work or information after a failure unless the canonical owner defines a terminal outcome.

#### 4. State and save

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture and restore the new fact, migrate older envelopes, make duplicate events idempotent, and keep optional content safe when its record is absent. Do not add a local counter merely to make the prose conditional.

#### 5. Deterministic replay

## Wave 47 supplemental receipt

The supplemental packets preserve the active twenty-field structure and broaden the playable content bank. They remain provisional until current catalog, ownership, save, replay, UI, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence is attached.

## Wave 47 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 47 extended depth packet 01: fox table compact at Amber Fox Horizon

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The fox table compact begins as a premise audit around Amber Fox Horizon. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Amber Fox Horizon, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Riverglass Beacon, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Riverglass Beacon notices labor and weather. A representative of Amber Fox Horizon Authority speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to South Finch Assembly remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Amber Fox Horizon Authority, South Finch Assembly, Riverglass Witnesses, and Grey Cinder Custodians by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Amber Fox Horizon Authority wants a reliable public record, South Finch Assembly protects a route custom, Riverglass Witnesses values a scarce repair skill, and Grey Cinder Custodians demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for fox table compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Grey Cinder Frontier, South Finch Causeway, Riverglass Witnesses, and Grey Cinder Custodians provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

### Wave 47 capsule 01: fox-window arbitration at Amber Fox Horizon

**Opening and choice.** At **Amber Fox Horizon**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Riverglass Beacon**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Grey Cinder Frontier**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **South Finch Causeway**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Amber Fox Horizon Authority** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **South Finch Assembly** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Riverglass Witnesses** values a scarce skill, while **Grey Cinder Custodians** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Amber Fox Horizon Authority**, **South Finch Assembly**, **Riverglass Witnesses**, and **Grey Cinder Custodians** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

#### 6. Location and shelter projection

Stage arrival, inspection, work, hazard, rest, departure, and return at Silver Rain Frontier. Add one physical trace, one shelter custom, one disputed memory, and one maintenance task so the location carries lore through action rather than exposition alone.

#### 7. Character and faction voice

Write distinct voices for a practical resident, an affected witness, and one representative of Mossglass Witnesses. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, refusal, apology, and late callback. Let a minor or absent voice receive a measurable consequence.

#### 8. Story and side-quest result

Build a side quest from an entry fact, one player action, one cost, one consequence, one refusal, one archive or journal fact, and a late-arrival variant. The scene may use prose, but the quest result must be an observable owner event that later content can read.

#### 9. UI and accessibility

Provide concise labels, expanded explanations, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, contrast, text scaling, non-color cues, irreversible-action confirmation, and a text or audio alternative. Long records must page or collapse without hiding the consequence.

#### 10. Performance and rollback

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, panel refresh, archive projection, and long text. Include a missing-data path, a rollback boundary, a focused contract check, a save round trip, and a host smoke only where the owner route requires it.
**Pass 526 receipt.** Accept The Recast Epilogue only when the owner, player result, failure behavior, save/replay fixture, and rollback note are written. The prose beat ends with an ordinary action: a lamp is trimmed, a pump is checked, a meal is shared, a coat is mended, a route marker is moved, or a record is read aloud. If that action cannot be wired to current authority, keep the packet as a design question.

## Wave 48 closeout receipt

## Wave 48 supplemental depth packets

These packets add volume to the current Wave 48 fields without introducing Fields 21–30. Each is a bounded design record for story, mechanics, systems, locations, shelter lore, character personalities, factions, late-game pressure, UI, persistence, replay, and performance.


### Supplemental packet 01: endgame horizons and legacy frontiers — Glasswater Beacon action 1

The scene opens at **Glasswater Beacon**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Glasswater Beacon, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **East Heron Assembly** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.

### Wave 48 extended depth packet 01: green table compact at Green Ash Horizon

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The green table compact begins as a premise audit around Green Ash Horizon. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Green Ash Horizon, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Glasswater Beacon, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Glasswater Beacon notices labor and weather. A representative of Green Ash Horizon Authority speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to East Heron Assembly remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Green Ash Horizon Authority, East Heron Assembly, Glasswater Witnesses, and Rust Bloom Custodians by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Green Ash Horizon Authority wants a reliable public record, East Heron Assembly protects a route custom, Glasswater Witnesses values a scarce repair skill, and Rust Bloom Custodians demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for green table compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Rust Bloom Frontier, East Heron Causeway, Glasswater Witnesses, and Rust Bloom Custodians provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Glasswater Beacon, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Glasswater Beacon notices labor and weather. A representative of Green Ash Horizon Authority speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to East Heron Assembly remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Green Ash Horizon Authority, East Heron Assembly, Glasswater Witnesses, and Rust Bloom Custodians by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Green Ash Horizon Authority wants a reliable public record, East Heron Assembly protects a route custom, Glasswater Witnesses values a scarce repair skill, and Rust Bloom Custodians demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

### Wave 48 capsule 01: green-window arbitration at Green Ash Horizon

**Opening and choice.** At **Green Ash Horizon**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Glasswater Beacon**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Rust Bloom Frontier**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **East Heron Causeway**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Green Ash Horizon Authority** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **East Heron Assembly** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Glasswater Witnesses** values a scarce skill, while **Rust Bloom Custodians** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Green Ash Horizon Authority**, **East Heron Assembly**, **Glasswater Witnesses**, and **Rust Bloom Custodians** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

### Supplemental packet 01: endgame horizons and legacy frontiers — Saltwater Beacon action 1

The scene opens at **Saltwater Beacon**, where the practical detail is more urgent than the ceremonial language: a damp ledger, a half-full water drum, a frayed coat, a relay key, a route marker, or an unlit lamp. A resident asks the player to inspect the public ledger. The player sees the cost before accepting and can refuse without losing the ability to return. The first response creates one canonical event and one journal or archive projection; later content reads that fact through the existing owner rather than through a panel cache.

**Mechanic and system contract.** Define the input, command, event key, result, refusal, fallback, and next choice. Use existing campaign, faction, relationship, roster, expedition, shelter, archive, or ending authority as appropriate. Stateful effects use the smallest current save section with capture, restore, migration, duplicate-event handling, and a seeded replay fixture. Do not create a second reputation score, route graph, relationship network, inventory ledger, calendar, or ending state. If the premise is absent in current source or data, keep this packet unresolved and record the exact missing seam.

**Location and shelter lore.** Explain who built Saltwater Beacon, what failed there, who repaired it, what custom grew from that repair, and who still pays its cost. Give the player one physical trace, one remembered phrase, one disputed interpretation, and one maintenance task. On a return visit, show the consequence before dialogue summarizes it. A quiet shelter detail should carry history: a bed rotated away from a draft, a cup reserved for visitors, a chalk line refreshed after rain, or a tool returned sharper than it was found.

**Character and faction direction.** The resident speaks plainly and notices labor before symbolism. A witness from **South Crane Assembly** uses formal language until a shortage makes the stakes concrete. A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

A third voice may be an apprentice, courier, absent person represented by an object, or elder who remembers a different version. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive one measurable outcome in the roster, route, archive, relationship, or ending projection.

**Story, UI, and verification.** The side quest needs an entry condition, player action, cost, consequence, refusal branch, archive fact, late-arrival variant, and missing-record variant. Prose should reveal the mechanic through ordinary work. The UI needs a compact label, expanded explanation, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible actions. Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, focused contract or data checks, save round trip, paired deterministic replay, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The packet is not an implementation claim; it is ready only for a safe-slice review.


## Wave 49 supplemental receipt

The supplemental packets preserve the active twenty-field structure and broaden the playable content bank. They remain provisional until current catalog, ownership, save, replay, UI, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence is attached.

## Wave 49 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 49 extended depth packet 01: willow table compact at Red Willow Horizon

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The willow table compact begins as a premise audit around Red Willow Horizon. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Red Willow Horizon, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Saltwater Beacon, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Saltwater Beacon notices labor and weather. A representative of Red Willow Horizon Authority speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to South Crane Assembly remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Red Willow Horizon Authority, South Crane Assembly, Saltwater Witnesses, and Indigo Cinder Custodians by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Red Willow Horizon Authority wants a reliable public record, South Crane Assembly protects a route custom, Saltwater Witnesses values a scarce repair skill, and Indigo Cinder Custodians demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for willow table compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Indigo Cinder Frontier, South Crane Causeway, Saltwater Witnesses, and Indigo Cinder Custodians provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

### Wave 49 extended depth packet 06: cinder bell covenant at Red Willow Horizon

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The cinder bell covenant begins as a premise audit around Red Willow Horizon. The player is asked to return with a corrected map, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Red Willow Horizon, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Saltwater Beacon, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. #### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

### Wave 49 capsule 01: willow-window arbitration at Red Willow Horizon

**Opening and choice.** At **Red Willow Horizon**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Saltwater Beacon**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Indigo Cinder Frontier**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **South Crane Causeway**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Red Willow Horizon Authority** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **South Crane Assembly** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Saltwater Witnesses** values a scarce skill, while **Indigo Cinder Custodians** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Red Willow Horizon Authority**, **South Crane Assembly**, **Saltwater Witnesses**, and **Indigo Cinder Custodians** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

## Wave 50 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 50 extended depth packet 01: lantern table compact at Red Lantern Horizon

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The lantern table compact begins as a premise audit around Red Lantern Horizon. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Red Lantern Horizon, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Slate Orchard Beacon, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Slate Orchard Beacon notices labor and weather. A representative of Red Lantern Horizon Authority speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to South Badger Assembly remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

A representative of Red Lantern Horizon Authority speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to South Badger Assembly remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Red Lantern Horizon Authority, South Badger Assembly, Slate Orchard Witnesses, and Cobalt Rain Custodians by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Red Lantern Horizon Authority wants a reliable public record, South Badger Assembly protects a route custom, Slate Orchard Witnesses values a scarce repair skill, and Cobalt Rain Custodians demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for cobalt bell covenant carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Cobalt Rain Frontier, South Badger Causeway, Slate Orchard Witnesses, and Cobalt Rain Custodians provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.

## Wave 50 capsule layer

These capsules extend the Wave 50 fields with additional playable scaffolds. Each remains provisional, owner-bound, and documentation-only.

### Wave 50 capsule 01: frostline arbitration at Red Lantern Horizon

**Opening and choice.** At **Red Lantern Horizon**, the player finds a practical problem that cannot be solved by rhetoric alone: a weather window is closing, a shared tool has two claimants, a missing person may be returning, a night signal is being misread, an apprentice is ready before the shelter is ready, a water ration has been counted twice, a quiet route carries an old debt, or a legacy object must be placed in another person’s hands. The player inspects the evidence, asks for consent, compares accounts, chooses a cost, defers, or leaves. The cost appears before commitment and a refusal keeps a safe return path.

**Authority and mechanic.** Route the action through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define one command, one event key, one resulting fact, one refusal result, one fallback, and one idempotency rule. A derived readiness view may combine existing standing, relationship, route, roster, shelter, archive, expedition, or ending facts, but it cannot become a second ledger or clock. The mechanic should make an ordinary task consequential: rescheduling a crossing changes who carries a tool, recording a signal changes which watch is asked to stand, or accepting a handover changes who is invited to the next meeting. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk version first.

**Place and shelter lore.** At **Slate Orchard Beacon**, describe the builder, the repair that saved the room, the person who still pays for that repair, and the mark that remains unexplained. At **Cobalt Rain Frontier**, place a contrasting trace: a patched hinge, a dry shelf, an erased route line, a bell rope, a teaching slate, or a bowl set aside. At **South Badger Causeway**, let a shelter custom make the history useful: a lamp is moved only after consent, a tool is returned sharpened, a guest cup is washed before dawn, or a route name is spoken once and then left unclaimed. Returning to the location shows a changed object before exposition.

**Characters and factions.** A resident speaks in concrete duties and notices who will carry the burden. A representative of **Red Lantern Horizon Authority** uses public language and wants an auditable result. A voice from **South Badger Assembly** protects a custom that looks inefficient until its history is heard. **Slate Orchard Witnesses** values a scarce skill, while **Cobalt Rain Custodians** asks who will witness the consequence after the player leaves. Give each voice a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and callback. The late-game factional version may convene a coalition, certify a passage, steward a shelter custom, or preserve a memory, but it may request and witness only through existing authorities.

**Story and prose.** The scene opens with one quiet sentence about work: “The rope is dry enough for one more crossing,” “The cup was left where the missing person could find it,” or “The bell was rung before anyone agreed.” The player’s response changes who performs the task, what the journal remembers, and which later character feels entitled to speak. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants. Use concrete objects, short silences, and a callback that makes the earlier mechanic visible without turning the packet into a lore lecture.

**Data and content volume.** Candidate rows carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Create arrival, inspection, task, hazard, rest, departure, return, calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, and late-arrival variants. Keep the names of **Red Lantern Horizon Authority**, **South Badger Assembly**, **Slate Orchard Witnesses**, and **Cobalt Rain Custodians** provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven. A missing optional row should collapse to a truthful unavailable state rather than alter the deterministic core.

**Persistence and replay.** Capture the smallest new fact through the existing save section. Define pre-action, committed, refused, interrupted, restored, migrated, and duplicate-event states. Pin the campaign seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation, including the late-arrival and missing-record cases. Do not use wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, locale-sensitive sorting, or hidden randomness in prose.

**UI, accessibility, and lifecycle.** Expose a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard/controller close and back, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, confirmation for irreversible actions, and text or audio alternatives. Panels consume owner projections and dispose listeners on close. High-volume rows load lazily and page without changing order. Set budgets for parse, query, dispatch, archive projection, refresh, and return visits; document the missing-provider path and the smallest eventual host smoke.

**Acceptance and handoff.** Accept the capsule only with premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and rollback. The handoff records untouched shared paths and labels the content as design scaffolding. The final image is small and physical: a cord retied, a cup passed over, a map corrected, a signal answered, a tool returned sharper, a meal divided, or a door left open because someone was asked first.

## Wave 51 supplemental receipt

The supplemental packets preserve the active twenty-field structure and broaden the playable content bank. They remain provisional until current catalog, ownership, save, replay, UI, accessibility, performance, and rollback evidence is attached.


## Wave 51 extended depth layer

This larger tranche adds six extended packets per plan. They deepen the active twenty fields while keeping all mechanics, catalog rows, factions, locations, shelter customs, and late-game institutions provisional and owner-bound.

### Wave 51 extended depth packet 01: two-seal petition compact at Red Lantern Horizon

#### Extended field 01 — Premise and canon

The two-seal petition compact begins as a premise audit around Red Lantern Horizon. The player is asked to count the lamps before opening the door, but the proposal remains provisional until current source, JSON authority, event producer, host consumer, and ownership ledger are cited. Record the nearest existing seam, the exact absent seam, and the collision to exclude. If the premise is already represented, fold the prose into that owner and retire this packet rather than creating a duplicate.

#### Extended field 02 — Player loop

The loop has six readable beats: arrive at Red Lantern Horizon, inspect a practical sign, hear a resident’s account, choose a cost, perform one visible task, and return after the next weather or duty turn. The choice can preserve, delay, redirect, or refuse the request. Show the consequence before explanation. A failure gives information or a bounded recovery task unless the canonical owner defines a terminal result.

#### Extended field 03 — System contract

Route the command through the current owner for endgame horizons and legacy frontiers. Define command, event key, inputs, output fact, refusal, fallback, idempotency, and consumer. The packet may touch faction standing, route access, roster duty, shelter archive, relationship, expedition, or ending interpretation only through those authorities. It may not create a private truce score, route graph, calendar, inventory, reputation counter, or parallel legacy record.

#### Extended field 04 — Mechanic

Introduce one mechanic that makes maintenance and trust interact: a concession opens a safer task, a late repair changes a route window, or an honest admission reduces a future surprise. The mechanic should have a threshold, a visible cost, a reversible preparation state, and a deterministic result. The player can test the boundary in a low-risk scene before committing to the late-game version.

#### Extended field 05 — Location lore

At Slate Orchard Beacon, describe who built the room, which flood or fire altered it, who kept the key, and why one wall remains unpainted. Give the player a physical trace, a remembered phrase, a disputed interpretation, and a maintenance action. Returning to the site should show an object moved, repaired, withheld, or shared before any dialogue summarizes the change.

#### Extended field 06 — Shelter lore

The shelter projection keeps a custom tied to the same fact: a cup reserved for a messenger, a bell rung only after consent, a cord tied around a tool, or a bench left open for the missing. The custom has a practical function and a social cost. Its archive text must name the worker who sustains it and the person who objects without reducing either voice to exposition.

#### Extended field 07 — Character voices

Write three distinct voices. A resident of Slate Orchard Beacon notices labor and weather. A representative of Red Lantern Horizon Authority speaks in careful public terms until the cost reaches a family or crew. A witness linked to South Badger Assembly remembers a different sequence. Give each a promise, fear, boundary, apology, refusal, and late callback. Let a minor voice receive a measurable roster, route, archive, or ending consequence.

#### Extended field 08 — Faction politics

The faction layer distinguishes Red Lantern Horizon Authority, South Badger Assembly, Slate Orchard Witnesses, and Cobalt Rain Custodians by resource, ritual, and risk rather than color. Red Lantern Horizon Authority wants a reliable public record, South Badger Assembly protects a route custom, Slate Orchard Witnesses values a scarce repair skill, and Cobalt Rain Custodians demands a future witness. None is automatically virtuous. Coalition progress is a projection of existing standing and event facts, with dissent and abstention preserved.

#### Extended field 09 — Story and prose

The side quest opens with an ordinary sentence: someone asks whether the lamp, map, ledger, meal, or signal can wait one more night. The player’s answer changes who performs the task and what is remembered. Use restrained prose, concrete objects, and one silence that another character interprets differently. Add calm, pressure, failure, recovery, refusal, late-arrival, and missing-record variants.

#### Extended field 10 — Late-game system

The late-game form is a major faction or frontier institution that can only appear after several owner-bound facts agree. It may convene a coalition, certify a route, steward a shelter custom, or carry a legacy signal. Its powers are bounded: it can request, witness, schedule, or interpret. It cannot rewrite history, bypass save ownership, or silently convert provisional prose into canon.

#### Extended field 11 — Data and catalog

Candidate content rows for two-seal petition compact carry schema_version, snake_case ID, owner, prerequisites, references, effects, fallback text, localization key, archive policy, retirement note, and missing-data behavior. Link every row to one canonical consumer and one command. Keep Cobalt Rain Frontier, South Badger Causeway, Slate Orchard Witnesses, and Cobalt Rain Custodians provisional until catalog aliases and reachability are proven.

#### Extended field 12 — Save and migration

Use the smallest existing save section. Capture the new fact, restore it, migrate older envelopes, tolerate an absent optional row, and make duplicate events idempotent. Define the pre-event, committed, refused, interrupted, and restored states. Do not encode prose branches in a panel cache. A rollback note must identify the event boundary and the owner responsible for undo or compensating projection.

#### Extended field 13 — Deterministic replay

Pin seed, event key, input order, and expected projection. Paired replays must agree on standing, access, route, roster, archive, or ending interpretation. Avoid wall-clock seeds, unordered iteration, hidden random choices, and locale-sensitive sorting. Include a late-arrival replay and a missing-record replay so optional content cannot alter the deterministic core unexpectedly.

#### Extended field 14 — UI and accessibility

The UI exposes a compact action label, expanded explanation, cost, consequence preview, focus order, keyboard and controller back behavior, readable long text, contrast, scaling, non-color cues, and confirmation for irreversible choices. Provide an audio or text alternative. If a record is missing, show a truthful unavailable state and preserve navigation. Archive and map panels consume projections; they do not own decisions.

#### Extended field 15 — Performance and lifecycle

Set budgets for catalog parse, query, event dispatch, archive projection, panel refresh, long text, and return visits. Load high-volume rows lazily, page them without changing order, dispose listeners on close, and avoid repeated full-catalog scans. Add one degradation path for a missing asset or provider. Note the smallest focused host smoke needed if the owner route is eventually implemented.

#### Extended field 16 — Acceptance and handoff

Acceptance requires premise evidence, owner and consumer proof, one reachable player command, save round trip, migration fixture, paired replay, accessibility review, performance notes, and a rollback boundary. The handoff names untouched shared paths and labels this as design scaffolding. The final image is practical: a repaired latch, an amended map, a divided bowl, a chalk mark, a quiet signal, or a door left open by consent.
